Wacker Chemie.why: Supplies semiconductor-grade (hyperpure) polysilicon to wafer manufacturers, mostly under long-term contracts; semiconductor-grade volumes grew about 10% in H1 2026 and management ties wafer-area growth to AI data-center demand.
Wacker Chemie.evidence: Wacker Chemie Q2 FY2026 (07-30-2026), CFO: 'What is growing nicely is our semiconductor business. We had seen roughly a 10% increase in the first half of this year.'

players.product: semiconductor-grade (hyperpure) polysilicon feedstock for silicon wafer manufacturers

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results: group sales EUR 1.52 billion versus EUR 1.41 billion a year earlier, driven by higher prices and volumes; EBITDA before the pension accounting effect up 53% to EUR 175 million from EUR 114 million; reported EBITDA EUR 211 million including a EUR 37 million non-cash pension effect; EBIT EUR 96 million; net income EUR 350 million (EPS EUR 6.86) including EUR 243 million of Siltronic-related effects (share sale and revaluation of the remaining stake). CEO: 'This was not a result of a broad market recovery. It was a result of actions within our control.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 sales EUR 1.52 billion; EBITDA before pension effect EUR 175 million (+53%); net income EUR 350 million

quarterly_data.signal: Polysilicon segment Q2: sales approximately EUR 226 million, up 3% year over year, as higher semiconductor-grade volumes offset lower solar-grade prices; EBITDA EUR 11 million, supported by strong semiconductor demand and cost savings but held back by solar pricing, higher energy costs and solar inventory destocking. CFO: semiconductor polysilicon grew roughly 10% in H1; Q2 semi-grade mix was weaker than Q1, but contract structures give a sequential improvement into H2, and most of the segment's profitability now comes from semiconductor and cost savings.
quarterly_data.figure: Polysilicon Q2 sales ~EUR 226 million (+3%); EBITDA EUR 11 million; semiconductor polysilicon roughly +10% in H1

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 guidance raised: group EBITDA EUR 625 million-EUR 750 million (on Q2 performance and the pension effect); capital expenditure approximately EUR 300 million with major expansion projects complete; net financial debt around EUR 500 million by year end. Polysilicon outlook lowered: sales up by a high single digit % with EBITDA close to the prior-year level, supported by double-digit % volume growth in semiconductor-grade polysilicon and savings offsetting substantially higher energy costs. Silicones and Polymers: mid-single-digit sales growth with EBITDA margins above prior year; Biosolutions: high single-digit sales growth, EBITDA around EUR 30 million.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 EBITDA EUR 625 million-EUR 750 million; capex ~EUR 300 million; net debt ~EUR 500 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: AI is driving semiconductor growth and ultimately wafer-area growth, though customers report a lag of up to one or two years from AI demand to wafers because of inventory; company analysis indicates a new data center may need four times the polysilicon of today's, which is why Wacker focuses its polysilicon strategy on semiconductors. CFO: semiconductor polysilicon is sold mostly under fixed long-term contracts, with some spot material for customers that do not want long-term contracts.
quarterly_data.figure: polysilicon per data center up to four times (company analysis)

quarterly_data.signal: Solar polysilicon: unresolved US Section 232 trade proceedings are holding back customer purchasing and volumes; polysilicon inventory is 20% lower than a year ago, with all three plants running at sub-efficient utilisation. CFO: if there were no solar option, Wacker would have one plant too many, but there is no pre-decision. Energy: large portions hedged for the rest of 2026 and roughly 75% for next year; a EUR 90 million headwind from lower CO2 compensation versus the prior year.
quarterly_data.figure: polysilicon inventory -20%; ~75% of 2027 energy hedged; EUR 90 million CO2 compensation headwind

quarterly_data.signal: Other segments Q2: Silicones sales EUR 757 million (+6%), EBITDA EUR 123 million; Polymers sales approximately EUR 406 million (+12%), EBITDA EUR 69 million including a low double-digit inventory valuation effect; Biosolutions sales EUR 99 million (+13%), EBITDA EUR 7 million. PACE cost programme: EUR 45 million in Q2 and EUR 85 million in H1, target of more than EUR 300 million savings by 2028, with an agreement to cut 1,600 positions in Germany. Equity EUR 4.18 billion, liquidity EUR 1.57 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: Silicones EUR 757 million; Polymers ~EUR 406 million; Biosolutions EUR 99 million; PACE savings EUR 85 million in H1
